We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON tree: root molecule, then reaction nodes each with template_id, children being precursor molecules (type mol). The route must be linear? At least 5 reactions, using those templates in order. So we need to apply each template sequentially to break down the target into precursors, ending with some simple molecules (maybe commercially available). We have attempted applying template 29646 to target, got three possible outcomes (three sets of products). Need to choose one that can be further processed by next template 1914389, etc.

We need to construct a chain: target -> after template 29646 gives some intermediate(s). Then apply 1914389 to one of those intermediates, etc.

We need to ensure each step is valid (template matches). The apply_template tool gave results; we need to pick a consistent path.

Let's examine first result from template 29646: It returned three possible outcomes (tuples). The result string: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO',))"

So three possible products each as a single molecule (since each tuple contains one string). The first product includes a silyl protecting group on the side chain (CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C). The second product has silyl on the acid group? Actually O[Si] attached to the carboxyl? The third product has silyl on the hydroxyl.

We need to then apply template 1914389 to one of these. We previously applied 1914389 to the first product (with silyl on side chain) and got result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),)". So that reaction splits into two products: one is a smaller molecule (still with silyl) and the other is an ester/ phosphonate? Actually "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That seems like a side product.

But we need a linear route: each reaction should produce precursors that become reactants for next step. Usually retrosynthesis splits target into simpler fragments; we need to continue breaking down the main fragment until we reach simple building blocks.

Thus after first reaction (29646) we have product A (the main fragment) and maybe side product(s). We can choose the main fragment to continue.

From 1914389 applied to product A gave two products: product B (C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C) and product C (CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC). We can continue with product B using next template 1914390.

We attempted applying 1914390 to product B and got empty result (no match). So maybe need to apply 1914390 to product C? Let's try.
